living.note: From Federico II's official presentation: utilities 100 – 150 € a month, food 200 – 300 €. The university itself does not provide dormitories. The overall budget is an estimate.

name: Bologna
intro: A classic student city: city life revolves around the university.
points: The ER.GO scholarship in 2026/27 is up to 7 171 €; the dormitory is paid from the scholarship.
Renting is hard: start looking early.

living.note: Room price from the University of Bologna's official page; overall budget estimated from rental websites.

name: Rome
intro: Italy's capital and largest student city. Sapienza, Tor Vergata, Roma Tre, LUISS and other universities are here.
pros: A wide choice of universities: state and private universities in one city.
Internships and jobs: ministries, embassies and UN organisations such as FAO, IFAD and WFP are based here.
History at every step: the city centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Mild climate: warm winters, lots of sunny days.
A strong scholarship: in 2026/27 DiSCo gave 6 571 – 7 556 € in cash and 2 free meals a day (about 8 157 € in total including meals).
Fiumicino: Italy's largest airport, flights all over the world.
cons: Rent is above the Italian average: look for housing early.
The city is big: getting to campus can take time, Tor Vergata is on the outskirts.
Queues at public offices can be long: start the permesso and other tasks early.

living.note: Sapienza recommends a minimum budget of at least 800 € (including rent); rental websites say 800 – 1 200 €. Cheaper in neighbourhoods like San Lorenzo and Pigneto, expensive in the centre.

intro: Italy's centre of finance, business and design. Università degli Studi di Milano, Politecnico di Milano and Bocconi are here.
points: The city with the strongest job market.
One of the most expensive cities in Italy to live in.
Each university announces the scholarship itself.

living.note: Politecnico di Milano's official estimate, excluding tuition. According to Bocconi, a private double room costs 500 – 750 €. Città Studi and Bovisa are cheaper.

intro: A city of industry and engineering, next to the Alps. Università di Torino and Politecnico di Torino are here.
points: Living is cheaper than in Rome and Milan.
The EDISU scholarship in 2026/27 is up to 8 097 € for fuori sede (8 455 € for women in STEM).

living.note: Room and transport prices from the University of Turin's official page; overall budget estimated from rental websites. City transport may be free for some students (Piemove programme), check the conditions.

intro: A seaside city in Sicily, on the Strait of Messina.
points: Tuition 156–506 € a year (depending on the country group).
Living in the south is usually cheaper.
The ERSU scholarship in 2026/27 is up to 8 246 €.

living.note: The University of Florence does not publish an official monthly amount; figures are estimates from rental websites. In university canteens prices are reduced according to family income (ISEE).

University of Pisa: a room costs on average 300 – 350 € + utilities (400 – 450 € with utilities). Landlords usually ask for a deposit of 2–3 months' rent. Overall budget per the Sant'Anna School's estimate.
